attributes.board_name: North Carolina Board of Physical Therapy Examiners

rules.accepted_credit_types: Points under 21 NCAC 48G .0109: live courses from approved providers 1 point per contact hour (max 29; interactive electronic max 15); non-interactive electronic courses and approved-provider home study 1 point/hour (max 10 each); post-baccalaureate academic course 15 points per semester hour (max 29); APTA-credentialed residency/fellowship 10 points per year (max 20); ABPTS specialty certification 20 points; FSBPT Practice Review Tool 10 points (5 if not passed); clinical instructor 1 point per 40 h (max 8); presenting/teaching 2 points/hour (max 6); research/publications (max 15); clinical practice 1-3 points per year by hours worked; Reflective Practice self-assessment 5 points; in-services (max 5); professional service and APTA membership (1 point/year). One contact hour = 50 consecutive minutes.
rules.new_licensee_rule: The reporting period starts on January 1 following the date of initial licensure.
rules.carryover: Up to 10 extra points may be carried to the next reporting period, except points for the Jurisprudence Exercise, Clinical Practice and Self-Assessment.
rules.audit_note: A Continuing Competence Reporting Form is submitted with the license renewal application; keep evidence 4 years after the reporting period. Random audits: documents due within 30 days of the Audit Notice.

topics.who: Board's online Jurisprudence Exercise every reporting period (1 point; max 3 points per period)

rules.notes: Licenses are renewed annually and expire January 31. Continuing competence is counted in points over a 25-month reporting period that begins on January 1 (two years plus the January renewal month). Most activities earn 1 point per 50-minute contact hour.
rules.rule_quote: (b) For individuals whose date of initial licensure is after January 1, 2009, commencing on January 1 following the date of initial licensure, each physical therapist must accumulate 30 points and each physical therapist assistant must accumulate 20 points of continuing competence activities during the reporting period to be eligible for license renewal.

rules.accepted_credit_types: Same point system as PT (21 NCAC 48G .0109); PTAs also earn 19 points per reporting period for APTA Advanced Proficiency designation for the PTA.
